sources: dossier=Net position + Storage section: 'A queued node_run pins its upstream RUNS ... at enqueue time via the wait-set row's sender_run_id; its substituted values must come from those pinned runs once settled ... wait-set rows signal which receiver to evaluate and carry no data (2026-06-23/2026-07-13, transcript)'; doc=lines 35/46/48 said substitution 'looks up ... against the wait-set sender runs that contributed to this dispatch'; code=substitution_context.go populateSubscribedSenderDeps reads GetMostRecentSettledRun in RunScope, no WaitSet() call, corroborated by decisions/substitution-deps-from-persisted-senders.md
note: Dossier (transcript tier, twice) establishes the wait-set entry only pins sender-run identity at enqueue and carries no attribute data; doc's 'looks up against the wait-set sender runs' framing implied the wait-set itself is a data source. Rewrote all three passages to the pinned-sender-run-at-enqueue model.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'Substitution runs in exactly two rounds on one uniform code path: upstream/attribute substitution at pending->stale (snapshotting), claim substitution at stale->running (2026-06-21, transcript)'; and 'A message node IS the message: its attributes are exactly the payload, copied verbatim with no receiver-side substitution (transcript)'; doc=line 47 claimed a single substitution moment per row; code=gate_evaluator.go defers claim./child. sources (sourceReferencesLateBound) to fillClaimRefs at dispatch; message_delivery.go copies payload verbatim with no substitution call at all
note: Dossier is unambiguous and transcript-tier: substitution is two rounds (pending->stale, then pre-dispatch for late-bound claim/child refs), and message-delivery rows get no substitution whatsoever. Doc's single-moment invariant contradicted both. Rewrote invariant 47 to the two-round model plus the message-delivery carve-out, and fixed a downstream inconsistency this created in the defaults-materialization note.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'Match observability is event-derived: each match emits an attribute_override_matched operational event at dispatch; the API aggregates counts from the event log at read time (2026-07-06, 3f71f90a, transcript)'; Intentional absences: 'Persisted attribute_overrides_match_counts column - dropped (migration 020); counts are event-derived at read time (transcript)'; doc=line 87 described counters persisting on the instance row's match-count map; code=migration 020 drops attribute_overrides_match_counts, emitOverrideMatchEventsAfterMerge emits events, CountAttributeOverrideMatchesByIndex derives counts
note: Dossier at transcript tier confirms the column was deliberately dropped and replaced by event-derived counting; doc named the dropped column's model as current. Rewrote the matcher-overlay match-count paragraph to the event-derived model (also resolves 519 and 1461, same passage).

sources: dossier=Required behaviors, Storage section: 'Fresh-scope defaults realize in two steps: empty bag written at row creation; effective bag ... computed and persisted at the substitution moment - pending->stale for cascade rows (2026-07-06, 3f71f90a, transcript)'; doc=line 69 (formerly 67) states the per-run attribute row is written with an empty bag at row creation and a not-yet-gated reader sees an empty bag; code=CreateCascadePending only inserts into rimsky_node_runs, no NodeAttributes().Upsert at creation, so GetByRun returns nil (absent row), not an empty bag
note: Dossier is transcript-tier and explicit: an empty bag should be written at row creation as step one of the two-step defaults model. The doc matches that intent exactly. Code instead writes no ledger row at all until the gate transition (nil vs empty is a real behavioral gap for any raw-ledger reader). Doc is correct against known intent; queued as fix-code, not touched here.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'Substitution runs in exactly two rounds ... upstream/attribute substitution at pending->stale (snapshotting)' (2026-06-21, transcript); env is grouped with the non-late-bound sources resolved in that first round per the same substitution-timing model used to fix row 10; doc=line 44 said host-environment variables are 'read from the supervisor process's environment at dispatch time', contradicting the doc's own substitution-timing invariant
